KidsHabits Privacy Policy

Effective date: 28 October 2026

Kids Habits is a chore, habit and rewards tracker for families, made by Reino Eterno. It is available for Android (on Google Play and the Amazon Appstore) and as a web app at kidshabits.reinoeterno.online. This policy explains what happens to your information when you use it.

The short version: Kids Habits has no ads, no analytics and no tracking, and never sells or shares your data. Unless you turn on Family Sync, everything stays on your device. If you do turn it on, your family’s data is stored on our server only so that your own devices can stay in step.

Kids Habits is meant to be used by parents and guardians. Children do not create accounts and do not need to give the app anything.

What the app stores on your device

Everything you enter is kept in a database inside the app on your device:

  • your children’s profiles — full name, nickname and date of birth (used only to show their age);
  • chores and habits — their names, points, the days they apply to, and timer lengths;
  • daily records — which chores were done, missed or timed out on each day;
  • rewards — the catalog you create, and the history of rewards redeemed;
  • bonus points and penalties you have given;
  • settings — language, the Second Chance option and, if you use Family Sync, the family code, family name and email address described below.

On the web version, the same database is saved in your browser’s local storage, so that reloading the page does not lose it. It stays in your browser.

None of this leaves your device unless you set up Family Sync. Uninstalling the app (or clearing the site’s data in your browser) deletes it.

On Android, if your device has system backup turned on, the operating system may include this database in your device backup (for example, your Google account backup). That copy is handled by your device’s backup service, not by us. You can turn it off in your device settings.

Family Sync (optional)

Family Sync lets several devices — two parents’ phones, a shared tablet, the web app — see the same chores, balances and rewards. It is off until you create or join a family.

When it is on, the app sends to our server:

  • all the family data listed above (children’s profiles, chores, daily records, rewards, redemptions, bonuses and penalties, and the synced settings: language, Second Chance, family name and email). Items you delete are marked as deleted on the server rather than erased, so that the deletion reaches your other devices and past records stay consistent;
  • a family code — a short random code that identifies your family group. Anyone who has the code can join the group and see its data, so share it only with people you trust;
  • a family name and an email address — the email is used to send you a 6-digit verification code. The code expires after 15 minutes and is discarded once used. We do not send any other email: no newsletters and no marketing;
  • a device identifier — a random ID created by the app, not your device’s hardware or advertising ID, so the server can tell your family’s devices apart;
  • a short device description — the device’s manufacturer and model and its operating-system version (on the web, the browser’s user-agent string), and when the device last synced. We use it only to recognise devices when troubleshooting a family’s sync.

Your data is visible to the devices in your family group and to the developer, who can access the server to keep the service running and to help when you ask for support. It is never shown to other families.

Technical information

When the app talks to our server, the server sees your device’s IP address, as every internet server does. Our hosting provider may record it, with the address requested and the time, in ordinary server logs, which are used only to run and secure the service. We do not store it in our database or use it for anything else.

All communication between the app and the server is encrypted with HTTPS.

No ads, no analytics, no tracking

  • There is no advertising and no advertising ID is used.
  • There are no analytics, crash-reporting, attribution or tracking tools, and no third-party SDKs that collect data.
  • We do not sell, rent or trade any information, and we do not profile you or your children.
  • There are no in-app purchases or subscriptions.

Permissions

On Android, Kids Habits asks for:

  • Internet — only used by Family Sync.
  • Notifications — to show a running chore timer, with Done and Stop buttons, and to tell you when the time is up.
  • Alarms & reminders (exact alarms) — so a timed chore ends exactly on time even when the device is idle.

The app does not access your contacts, location, photos, files, camera or microphone.

Who else is involved

The sync server and the web app are hosted by DreamHost, a United States company, which also delivers the verification email. It processes the data only to provide hosting for us. If you live outside the United States, using Family Sync means your family’s data is stored there.

How long we keep things

  • On your device: until you delete it or uninstall the app.
  • On the server: for as long as your family group exists. Verification codes expire after 15 minutes.
  • Server logs: kept for the short period our hosting provider retains them, and used only to operate and secure the service.

Deleting your data

  • To delete the data on a device, uninstall the app (on the web, clear the site’s data in your browser).
  • To delete your family’s data from our server, email contact@kidshabits.reinoeterno.online from the address you verified in the app, or include your family code. We will delete the family group and everything stored with it — profiles, records, rewards, settings, email address and device records — within 30 days, and confirm when it is done.

Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access a copy of your data, to correct it, to have it deleted, and to object to how it is used. In Brazil the LGPD gives you these rights; in the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom, the GDPR does. Parents in the United States have the corresponding rights under COPPA for their children’s information. To use any of them, write to the address below and we will answer within 30 days.

Children

Kids Habits is used by parents and guardians on behalf of their family. A child’s name, nickname and date of birth are entered by the parent, and are used only to show the child’s chores, points and age inside the family’s own app. We do not collect information directly from children, and children are never asked to sign in or give an email address. If you believe a child has given us information without a parent’s consent, contact us and we will delete it.

Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, the new version will be published at this same address with a new effective date. Significant changes will also be mentioned in the app’s release notes.

Contact

Questions about this policy or your data: Adam Foerster, contact@kidshabits.reinoeterno.online.
